briefing:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The Middle East faces significant escalation as Iran claimed missile strikes on the UAE, while concurrently, Tehran's Parliament Speaker declared the Strait of Hormuz closed until economic sanctions are lifted, directly contradicting US President Trump's assertion of an open waterway and no planned talks. Meanwhile, Israel repatriated the remains of a soldier missing since 1982 and conducted strikes against Hamas commanders in Gaza.

IRAN
Iran's Ministry of Defense announced two ballistic missiles were fired towards the UAE, with one impacting within Emirati territorial waters. Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi stated that US President Trump's "delusion" regarding the Strait of Hormuz as US territory would be corrected by Iran. Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf declared that the Strait of Hormuz would remain closed until oil sanctions are lifted, frozen assets are released, the US blockade ends, and military threats cease, adding that Iran is prepared for a heavier defeat if hostilities resume.

Separately, Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi informed mediators that Iran does not accept a ceasefire but demands an end to the war, asserting that the conflict must conclude in a manner that prevents its recurrence. He also claimed a "post-American order" is emerging in the Persian Gulf, and that countries not hosting US bases were less affected by the recent conflict. Iran's national gas company reported that 60-70% of its gas industry, damaged during "American-Zionist" attacks, has returned to production. Anonymous Iranian officials, speaking to Reuters, expressed concerns that escalating US economic sanctions could worsen public discontent and lead to renewed nationwide protests against the regime. Additionally, Iran's Defense Ministry affirmed its commitment to advancing military capabilities in line with the "martyred Leader's legacy." The IRGC deputy chief claimed Iranian air defense systems shot down over 200 enemy aircraft during the recent US-Israeli aggression. Iran announced plans to build the world's largest solar plant, a 5,000 MW facility in Isfahan. Iran also issued warnings to shipping companies against supporting US military operations.

ISRAEL
The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) confirmed the repatriation of the remains of Sgt. First Class Yehuda Katz, who went missing during the 1982 First Lebanon War's Battle of Sultan Yacoub. This operation, led by IDF Military Intelligence and the Mossad, marks the completion of the mission to return all missing soldiers from that battle.

In Gaza, the IDF conducted an aerial strike near Gaza City port, targeting Hamas Nukhba commanders who were planning attacks against Israeli forces. The IDF stated that one of the eliminated commanders had participated in the October 7, 2023, attack on Israeli territory. Palestinian media reports indicate that this strike hit a cafe, killing six people, including a child, and wounding ten others. The IDF also announced the elimination of Tareq Anwar Khamis Ra'i, an Islamic Jihad company commander, in Khan Younis on Sunday. Ra'i was identified as having participated in the October 7 attack on Kibbutz Be'eri and the abduction of an Israeli civilian. Defense Minister Yoav Gallant reiterated Israel's policy in Gaza: "removing threats, eliminating terrorists, and exacting retribution for all who participated in the October 7 massacre."

Regarding Syria, an Israeli official claimed that an overnight strike on the Abu al-Zuhour Military Airport near Idlib was intended to prevent Turkish military entrenchment in the area. US President Trump's envoy, Tom Burke, publicly criticized this strike as an "unnecessary escalation." Israel also confirmed sharing "sensitive intelligence" with the US prior to the Syria strike. On the home front, the IDF's 190th Squadron, operating AH-64A Apache helicopters, is relocating from Ramon Airbase in the south to Ramat David Airbase in the north. The Attorney General's Office recommended expanding financial enforcement measures against ultra-Orthodox draft evaders and advised the military and police to resume arrests to enforce equality in military service. Marketing has begun for approximately 1,400 housing units in the E1 area, aimed at connecting Ma'ale Adumim to Jerusalem.

GAZA & WEST BANK
Israeli forces conducted an aerial strike near the Gaza City port against Hamas Nukhba commanders planning attacks; Palestinian media reported six fatalities, including a child, and ten wounded. The IDF confirmed that one of the eliminated commanders participated in the October 7, 2023, attack. The IDF also killed Tareq Anwar Khamis Ra'i, an Islamic Jihad company commander, in Khan Younis on Sunday, citing his involvement in the October 7 attack on Kibbutz Be'eri and abduction of an Israeli civilian, as well as advancing recent attacks against Israeli forces.

In the West Bank, Israeli settlers were reported to remain on a hill near Qusra, south of Nablus, despite an announced evacuation operation, with footage showing them interacting with Israeli soldiers. Separately, Israeli forces demolished a Palestinian house in al-Khalil and settlers reportedly attacked a Red Crescent Society ambulance transporting a patient in the same area. A kite with Arabic writing was found in the Simhoni Forest near the Gaza perimeter. Negotiations regarding Gaza's future are uncertain, with the Board of Peace reportedly considering a demand for a wholesale Hamas weapons handover before any Israeli withdrawal, a shift from previous phased disarmament proposals.

LEBANON
The remains of Sgt. First Class Yehuda Katz, missing since the 1982 First Lebanon War battle of Sultan Yacoub, were successfully returned to Israel, closing a 44-year search. The Lebanese Army Commander, General Rudolf Hikal, condemned ongoing Israeli military attacks and violations of the Framework Agreement, without providing specific details of recent incidents. Hezbollah released a video titled "Walk in the name of God."

SYRIA & IRAQ
An American soldier was killed in northern Iraq on July 18, as announced by CENTCOM. In Syria, unidentified fighter jets, suspected to be Israeli, targeted the runway of Abu al-Zuhour Military Airport near Idlib. Turkish sources reported that this strike occurred just hours after a Turkish military delegation visited the site for runway restoration assessment, leading Turkey's Foreign Ministry to condemn the attack as Israeli. An Israeli official claimed the strike aimed to prevent Turkish military entrenchment. Trump's envoy, Tom Burke, expressed "grave concern" over the Israeli airstrikes, labeling them an "unnecessary escalation" that does not promote regional stability.

The Syrian Foreign Minister, Assad al-Shibani, stated that nuclear material found in a Syrian facility is "not dangerous" and will remain in Syria under IAEA supervision for potential civilian use. UN inspectors, for the first time, visited the Syrian reactor previously bombed by Israel and the secret Site 99, used for storing nuclear material.
In Iraq, a massive explosion was reported in Sulaymaniyah, with columns of smoke visible, but the cause remains unclear. The Iraqi Kata'ib Hezbollah resistance group set the full withdrawal of US forces as a condition for placing its weapons under state control. Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf is scheduled to visit Iraq to discuss regional developments and strengthen strategic cooperation. Nouri al-Maliki, head of Iraq's State of Law Coalition, informed the US Chargé d'affaires that Iraqi state institutions are the sole authority for managing security files and monopolizing weapons. There are reports that Russia is shipping drone components, ammunition, and TNT to Iran via the Caspian Sea to help Tehran replenish stockpiles damaged by US and Israeli strikes. Separately, the US Justice Department indicted 17 Iranians for a widespread cyber campaign to steal data from 144 US universities, 178 foreign universities, 42 companies, and government agencies.

GULF STATES
The UAE Ministry of Defense reported that two ballistic missiles were launched from Iran towards the UAE; one fell outside its territorial waters, and the other landed within. UAE President Mohammed bin Zayed held a phone call with US President Trump to discuss the situation in the Middle East. The British Maritime Trade Organization (UKMTO) reported that a cargo ship was hit by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz while transiting near Oman, causing damage to its starboard side and injuring one crew member. The Yemeni Houthis claimed a drone attack on a Saudi Aramco oil facility in Jizan, Saudi Arabia.

Saudi Arabia and the UAE are reportedly increasing their oil reserves in Japan and South Korea as a protective measure against potential disruptions from fighting in the Gulf. Separately, Saudi Arabia has placed financial transfers to the UAE under enhanced anti-crime oversight, a move reportedly linked to UAE's backing of secessionist forces in Yemen and disagreements over the Iran war response. The Emirate of Kuwait experienced a complete power outage in the Abdullah al-Salem district for unknown reasons. Qatar's Foreign Ministry indicated that envoys are awaiting a bilateral agreement between Oman and Iran on a safe transit route through the Strait of Hormuz before resuming broader US-Iran negotiations. Oil prices have reportedly increased due to disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Iranian Missile Strike on UAE:** The UAE Ministry of Defense reported that two ballistic missiles were launched from Iran, with one impacting within UAE territorial waters, prompting forces to be on full alert.
2.  **Hormuz Closure Threat & US Contradiction:** Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf declared the Strait of Hormuz would remain closed until oil sanctions are lifted, frozen assets released, the US blockade ends, and military threats cease. This directly contradicts US President Trump's statements reaffirming an open Strait, naval blockade, and his declaration of Hormuz as "new US Territory."
3.  **Israeli Soldier's Remains Repatriated:** The remains of Israeli Sgt. First Class Yehuda Katz, missing since the 1982 First Lebanon War, were recovered and returned to Israel after a 44-year effort by the IDF Military Intelligence Directorate and Mossad.
4.  **Gaza Strike against Hamas Commanders:** The IDF conducted an aerial strike near the Gaza City port, targeting Hamas Nukhba commanders planning attacks. Palestinian media reported 6 fatalities, including a child, and 10 wounded.
5.  **Israeli Airstrike in Syria:** Unidentified fighter jets, suspected to be Israeli, targeted the runway of Abu al-Zuhour Military Airport near Idlib, Syria. Turkey condemned the strike, while an Israeli official claimed it aimed to prevent Turkish military entrenchment. Trump's envoy, Tom Burke, criticized the strike as an "unnecessary escalation."
6.  **Pentagon Reassesses ME Presence:** The Pentagon is re-evaluating its military presence in the Middle East after the Iran war, with CENTCOM Commander Brad Cooper supporting a potential reduction in Persian Gulf deployments and relocation of forces westward.
7.  **Russia Arming Iran:** Russia is reportedly shipping drone components, ammunition, and TNT to Iran via the Caspian Sea to replenish stockpiles damaged by US and Israeli strikes.
8.  **US Sanctions on ICC Officials:** The United States imposed sanctions on International Criminal Court (ICC) President Tomoko Akane and Judge Abdoulaye Saye.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
ESCALATION RISKS: The direct missile launch from Iran towards the UAE represents a significant and immediate escalation, with the UAE maintaining full alert. The explicit contradiction between Iran's declared intent to close the Strait of Hormuz and US President Trump's insistence on its openness creates a high-risk flashpoint for maritime confrontation. Israeli airstrikes deep within Syria, especially following a Turkish military visit to the target site, risk drawing in Turkey and further destabilizing the region, exacerbated by the US envoy's public criticism. The reported Russian supply of military components to Iran via the Caspian Sea could enhance Iran's ability to sustain conflict, prolonging the war's duration and intensity. Internal pressures and potential for renewed protests in Iran, as reported by Reuters, pose an additional risk of regime instability that could spill over regionally.

ACTIVE FLASHPOINTS: The Strait of Hormuz remains a critical flashpoint, characterized by direct Iranian threats, US counter-declarations, and recent maritime incidents including a cargo ship being struck. Gaza continues to be an active conflict zone with ongoing Israeli strikes against Hamas commanders and reported Palestinian casualties. Syrian airspace, particularly around Idlib, is volatile due to Israeli airstrikes and regional condemnation. The Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab are still threatened by Houthi operations, evidenced by the cargo ship damaged near Mocha, Yemen.

MILITARY POSTURE CHANGES: The UAE is on full alert following the missile attack. The IDF's 190th Apache Squadron is relocating to a northern base, indicating a strategic re-positioning. The Pentagon is actively considering a reduction and westward shift of US military forces in the Persian Gulf post-Iran war. Simultaneously, the USS Washington, a US nuclear aircraft carrier, is approaching the Arabian Sea, signifying a reinforced US naval presence. NATO aircraft activity around Kaliningrad and the Baltic Sea, including electronic warfare and ISR assets, indicates heightened readiness in a separate but related theater of global tensions. Iran's Defense Ministry has vowed to advance its military capabilities, suggesting continued strategic development.

RED LINES: Iran has explicitly stated it will not accept a ceasefire but demands a complete end to the war. Israel's policy in Gaza remains focused on eliminating threats, targeting terrorists, and seeking retribution for the October 7 attacks. US President Trump's red line for Iran is clear: "Iran cannot and will not have nuclear weapons." Iran's declaration that Hormuz will remain closed until sanctions are lifted, funds released, and military threats cease establishes a significant red line for economic and military pressure.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
US POSTURE: US President Trump declared "no talks or discussions" are ongoing or planned with Iran, contradicting anonymous US officials who claimed "positive talks" had occurred but Trump decided to wait. Trump reaffirmed the naval blockade and stated the Strait of Hormuz is open and active, while also rhetorically claiming it as "new US Territory." He criticized South Korea for not offering aid in Iran operations. The US Ambassador to Israel suggested Trump's unpredictable decisions on Iran aim to keep adversaries off balance. The Pentagon is re-evaluating its military presence in the Middle East post-Iran war, with CENTCOM Commander Brad Cooper supporting a potential reduction in Persian Gulf deployments and a westward relocation of forces. The US imposed sanctions on International Criminal Court (ICC) President Tomoko Akane and Judge Abdoulaye Saye. Trump's envoy, Tom Burke, publicly criticized an Israeli airstrike in Idlib, Syria, as an "unnecessary escalation." The US Justice Department indicted 17 Iranians for large-scale cyberattacks targeting US entities. Reuters/Ipsos polling indicates Trump's popularity is at a low point (33% approval), with 64% dissatisfied, and concerns over the duration of the Iran war impacting Republican midterm election prospects.

GULF STATES: The UAE's Ministry of Defense confirmed two ballistic missiles were launched from Iran towards its territory, prompting full alert. UAE President Mohammed bin Zayed discussed the Middle East situation with US President Trump. Qatar's Foreign Ministry stated that envoys are waiting for an Oman-Iran agreement on a safe transit route through the Strait of Hormuz before resuming broader US-Iran negotiations. Saudi Arabia has reportedly imposed enhanced anti-crime oversight on financial transfers to the UAE, due to disagreements over Yemen and the Iran war response. Yemen's Houthis claimed a drone attack on a Saudi Aramco facility in Jizan.

EU MEMBERS: France announced it would expel two Iranian diplomats after two French diplomats were "scandalously" attacked on July 19. German lawmakers have called for EU sanctions against Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir over remarks advocating for the killing of Gazans.

RUSSIA: Russia lodged a "strong protest" with Japan's ambassador over "anti-Russian statements" regarding President Putin's visit to the Kuril Islands. NBC News reported that Russia is shipping drone components, ammunition, and TNT to Iran via the Caspian Sea to help replenish Iran's stockpiles. Russia also reported downing 791 Ukrainian drones, with 620 near Moscow, and accused Ukraine of impeding IAEA visits to the Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant. Russian companies have requested government protection against drone attacks.

CHINA: Two major Chinese shipping companies have halted sending oil tankers through the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab. Chinese President Xi Jinping is expected to limit his September US visit to a meeting with President Trump, skipping the UN General Assembly.

TURKEY: Turkey's Foreign Minister condemned an Israeli airstrike on Abu al-Zuhour Military Airport in Syria. President Erdogan spoke with President Trump, urging continued negotiations with Iran for an agreement, and discussed the Gaza conflict and a defense pact between Turkey, Saudi Arabia, and Pakistan. Erdogan reportedly told Trump that Israeli attacks on Palestinians in Gaza had intensified as the second phase of Trump's peace plan was meant to take effect. Turkey's significant influence in Somalia was noted, with a Somali MP stating, "Erdogan does as he pleases."

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
CONTRADICTIONS BETWEEN SOURCES: A notable contradiction exists between US President Trump's explicit statement, "no talks or discussions" are ongoing or planned with Iran, and claims from an anonymous US official (reported by Shargh and Omid Dana) that "positive talks" with Iran occurred but Trump decided to wait. This discrepancy casts doubt on the current state of US-Iran diplomatic engagement.

Another significant contradiction arises regarding the Strait of Hormuz: while US President Trump unequivocally states the Strait is "open and active" and all naval mines have been "removed or detonated," Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf declared it would remain closed until specific Iranian demands are met, and reports indicate ongoing ship attacks and disruptions.

Press TV's claim that "alleged missile attacks on UAE inaccurate; Iran only claims actions it actually takes" directly contradicts the UAE Ministry of Defense's official statement that two ballistic missiles were launched from Iran towards the UAE, with one landing in its territorial waters.

UNVERIFIED CLAIMS: The statements from Omid Dana, such as "IRGC to attack US in few weeks" and "Iran plan for 3rd war," are highly speculative and lack official confirmation. US President Trump's pronouncement, "Strait of Hormuz - New US Territory," appears in multiple sources, but its official status is dubious and likely rhetorical, not legal. A report by Press TV attributing a call for Israel to halt attacks in Gaza to "US President Donald Trump" is anachronistic if Trump is currently President, given his other statements; this might be a misattribution or a reference to an older statement by a different official. The precise nature and quantity of "nuclear material" found in Syria, beyond "tons" (IAEA), remain broadly reported.

PROPAGANDA INDICATORS: Iranian state media (Press TV, Shargh) and affiliated channels frequently employ strong, defiant rhetoric emphasizing Iranian resilience and military capabilities while highlighting perceived US and Israeli failures, often framing events as "post-American order" or "Iran WON THE WAR." Omid Dana's channel consistently uses highly charged, speculative language and promotes narratives supportive of the "resistance axis," even in the context of casualties. Statements from Iranian officials often contain strong assertions of sovereignty and power projection.

REPORTING GAPS: Specific details regarding the cargo ship attack in the Strait of Hormuz—including the vessel's flag, precise cargo, origin, and destination—are not provided across sources. Independent verification of the number of casualties and precise circumstances of the Gaza strikes is lacking. The exact commitments and signatories of the "Islamabad MoU," frequently referenced by Iranian officials, are not detailed.
